issue.title: Concurrent bead sync can silently delete an event from a shared event stream, wedging every later sync
issue.description:
Discovered by epic phase agent sase-l1.5 (epic sase-l1, 2026-08-13) while landing unrelated monitor-visibility work.

Commit 32edc3208cac352165ab7d7b6d4d6f23d17f6ce6 in the shared beads store ("chore(beads): sync bead state and pages for sase-l3", agent bbugyi200.athena.sase-l3.1) silently deleted the last line of events/streams/sase-l1.jsonl on origin/main -- event 000040, a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note -- and added nothing back. Origin was then missing content present in the merge-base, so every subsequent 'sase bead sync' from that workspace failed with:

  ValueError: validation: cannot merge non-append-only bead event stream sase-l1: theirs missing base event 40

raised from src/sase/bead/conflict_resolver.py:_resolve_bead_conflicts. 'sase bead doctor' reported 11 consecutive failed managed-sync integrations before it was diagnosed by hand.

Two distinct defects:

1. ROOT CAUSE (unknown): whatever produced that 'sync bead state and pages' commit dropped a line from an append-only stream. Reproduce or bound the race in the sync/publish path; a bead event stream must never shrink.

2. DIAGNOSTICS: 'sase bead doctor' reports only the symptom (failed managed-sync integrations). It should detect the actual corruption -- a stream in origin that is shorter than its own history, i.e. missing events present in an ancestor commit -- and name the offending commit, so an agent does not have to run 'git log <base>..origin/main -- events/streams/<id>.jsonl' by hand.

The append-only check itself is behaving correctly: it refuses to silently drop history. Recovery required manually confirming origin added no new content and force-resolving to the local (superset) side before 'sase bead resolve-conflicts' could regenerate issues.jsonl.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-f0 — an adjacent bead-sync wedge (duplicate bead-id allocation) whose fix touched the same sync/conflict path; worth reading before changing conflict_resolver.py.

RESULT: append-only stream guard is at the commit/push boundary. prepare_event_streams_for_commit() in src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity.py compares each changed events/streams/*.jsonl to HEAD before commit_sdd_files and _commit_bead_state; pure shrinks restore the ancestor (and keep local extras as a valid superset), prefix rewrites restore ancestor bytes and raise BeadStreamIntegrityError, whole-file deletions still commit for bead rm, and relocation into a new stream remains allowed. refuse_unpublished_event_stream_shrink() blocks a generated sync/push of a committed shrink vs merge-base/upstream. diagnose_event_stream_history() is read-only on bead_sync_diagnostics/doctor and names the stream, missing/rewritten event range, and first offending commit (degrades if history is shallow/unavailable). Verified: tests/test_bead/test_stream_integrity.py plus conflict/publication/sync-worker/doctor suites; just test-scoped escalated (core-identity-changed) and passed 30617 tests / 11 skipped. just check lint otherwise passed (fmt, ruff, mypy, validate); pre-existing symvision private-import errors in models_panel_provider_* / vcs_log / bead.project._now were not introduced here. Land agent can close this task as done.

CLOSEOUT sase-mi.7: append-only event-stream guards in src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity.py and commit/push call sites remain verified after combined cleanup; test batch passed 66/66 across stream_integrity, sync recovery/worker, diagnostics, and bead page publication. Selected-fix Symvision public-helper findings were resolved by privatizing test-only stream helpers. just check now stops only at unrelated ready task sase-mn (FilesQueryIndexResult).

Fixed by epic sase-mi phase 2 (commit b681d1bc3). prepare_event_streams_for_commit in src/sase/bead/_stream_integrity.py now guards both bead-store commit paths (sdd/_commit_store.py, bead/_sync_git.py): a pure shrink restores the ancestor, a valid local superset is preserved, and a prefix rewrite restores ancestor bytes and raises BeadStreamIntegrityError; whole-file deletion still commits for bead rm and relocation into a new stream stays allowed. refuse_unpublished_event_stream_shrink guards the push in sync_worker.py against merge-base/upstream. Both defects in this bead are covered: diagnose_event_stream_history feeds bead doctor / sync diagnostics and names the stream, the missing or rewritten event range, and the first offending commit -- verified live, sase bead doctor now reports this bead's own case as 'bead event stream sase-j7 is shorter than its own history: missing events 62-63 present in ancestor 7e3d27461b3a; first offending commit 812e352b4def', which previously required running git log by hand. Verified at HEAD daf933aa5 by the landing agent: tests/test_bead/test_stream_integrity.py plus the conflict, publication, sync-worker, recovery, and doctor suites are green inside a 381-test focused batch. Residual work is tracked separately and is not this defect: sase-ms (settled historical rewrites should classify below ERROR so a new one stands out) and sase-mr (write_event_store re-serializes every stream on every mutation, which is why one bad stream could abort an unrelated bead's write).
